note: Attacker-controlled input size Size is used to create a malloc:// IO descriptor of that size, establishing the memory buffer bounds.
Attacker-controlled bytes Data are written into the malloc:// buffer at offset 0, so the buffer content is fully attacker-controlled.
The 'ia' command triggers binary info parsing which issues reads through the IO layer, passing attacker-influenced read lengths to io_memory_read.
The read length len (derived from parsed binary header fields) is forwarded to the plugin read function without bounds checking against the destination buffer.
The attacker-influenced len is passed unchanged to the io_memory plugin's read callback.
Vulnerability: memset writes count bytes to the caller's stack buffer before count is clamped to the malloc size, causing a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE when count exceeds the buffer capacity.
